ops.title: Codex parsing is typed but lenient
ops.body:
# Codex parsing is typed but lenient

`rust/crates/core/src/codex/` lifts OpenAI Codex CLI rollout JSONL into a typed superset model (`CodexEntry`), but parsing NEVER fails a file and NEVER panics on any input. The policy, in order of authority:

## Two-level fallthrough, raw always preserved
- A malformed line or unknown top-level `type` becomes the top-level `Other` with the raw line preserved (`from_utf8_lossy` is the accepted representation — byte-exact `Vec<u8>` raw was considered and rejected; invalid UTF-8 only arises from disk corruption).
- A `response_item`/`event_msg` whose payload `type` is unknown becomes that payload's `Other`, raw payload preserved.
- A KNOWN payload type stays typed under lenient `Option` extraction — a missing or oddly-typed *optional* field yields `None`, never `Other`. Only the **required-field sets** degrade a known type to payload-`Other`: `message` → `content` must be an array; `function_call`/`custom_tool_call` → string `call_id` + `name`; `*_output` → string `call_id`. Do NOT widen these sets: a future optional field with a surprising type must not nuke a row.

## Identity folding
Identity comes from the first `session_meta` row whose `id` extracts as a non-empty string; invalid rows never win or block the fold (identity-poisoning guard). Files may carry N `session_meta` rows (~50% of codex_exec files have a two-row head; one corpus outlier re-injects mid-stream) — later rows never overwrite. `SessionMeta` keeps its full raw payload alongside the typed identity fields, so unmodeled metadata (`context_window`, `history_mode`, `multi_agent_version`, …) is never dropped.

## Style and verification bar
- Manual `sonic_rs::Value` navigation with the `value.rs` helpers — NO serde in the production dep graph (serde is dev-only via criterion). Match this, not derive-macro style.
- Envelope timestamps parse via the shared lenient RFC3339 helper. Strict grammar validation (`.mmmZ` only) was considered and REJECTED: codex's writer makes offset forms structurally unreachable, and a narrow grammar would turn every line into `Other` if a future version widened subsecond precision.
- `function_call.arguments` and `custom_tool_call.input` stay VERBATIM strings — interpretation belongs to the typed tool-call layer, never the parser.
- Some variants are recognized-but-raw (named enum variants holding their raw payload: `TurnContext`, `GhostSnapshot`, low-frequency event kinds) — field-type them only when a consumer needs the fields.
- The regression bar: the fixture suite in `tests/testdata/codex/` must parse with exact per-variant tallies and produce ZERO top-level or payload-level `Other`, and a 400-file real-corpus smoke (throwaway `#[ignore]` test, deleted after; report aggregate stats only, never content) must show 0 panics and ~0% fallthrough. If payload-`Other` rises on current-version files, typed variants are missing fields.

Format ground truth lives in the note "Codex rollout format spec — P0 verification findings" (source rust-v0.144.5 + 4790-file corpus).
ops.when: read this when changing codex transcript parsing or event typing
